description: Issue #982: neutralizes the Authorization-add-point log-leak fix in WTMContext.CallApi.cs's CallAPI<T>, a scope gap in #979 (not a new defect -- #979 narrowed the exception path for the caller-supplied `headers` loop but left this sibling add-point, fed from LoginUserInfo?.RemoteToken, unprotected; the byte-for-byte identical gap in Services/WtmApiClient.cs's `authToken`-fed add-point is fixed in the same #982 commit but deliberately not covered by a second mutant here -- see below). This mutant re-widens the #982 narrow catch back into a leak by replacing the sanitized `throw new InvalidOperationException(...)` with a bare `throw;`, which rethrows the ORIGINAL FormatException unmodified. For the Authorization header .NET's own FormatException.Message embeds the FULL raw attempted 'Bearer <token>' value; that original exception then reaches the method's pre-existing, UNCHANGED broad catch (Exception ex), which hands it whole to WtmDiagnosticLogger.LogError(ex, ...) -- so a logging sink that renders Exception.ToString() (the .NET default) puts the secret back into application logs, reproducing the #982/#979 defect verbatim. DECOUPLING ARGUMENT for green_test (required by .claude/rules/testing.md 'A mutant's positive control must not touch the mutated decision path'): the chosen green_test is WtmContextCallApiHeaderLogLeakTests979.CallAPI_non_header_exception_is_still_handled_by_the_broad_catch_unchanged (the SAME test #979's own mutant entry uses as its green_test, reused here rather than either of the two new #982 tests). Trace: that test builds its WTMContext via MockWtmContext.CreateWtmContext() and never sets wtm.LoginUserInfo, so the LoginUserInfo property getter (WTMContext.User.cs) returns null (no authenticated HttpContext.User, no _remotetoken query parameter configured on the mock request) -- meaning LoginUserInfo?.RemoteToken is also null. The outer guard this mutant's catch block sits inside, `string.IsNullOrEmpty(LoginUserInfo?.RemoteToken) == false`, therefore evaluates to false for every invocation this test makes, so the entire `if` block -- including the try/catch this mutant patches -- is NEVER ENTERED for this test's call path. This is the strongest form of decoupling from the testing.md checklist (the call graph never reaches the mutated line at all), not a short-circuit or invariant-equality argument. The two #982-specific tests were deliberately NOT used as green_test: WtmContextCallApiAuthorizationHeaderLogLeakTests982.CallAPI_still_logs_the_rejected_Authorization_header_name asserts on output produced by the SAME catch block this mutant rewrites (Authorization's FormatException.Message never names the header, exactly the #979 POSITIVE_CONTROL_FAILED shape already documented in docs/production-readiness.md and .claude/rules/testing.md) and would fail under this mutant for a reason unrelated to being a valid control. The sibling defect in src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Services/WtmApiClient.cs (byte-for-byte the same shape, same fix, fixed in the same #982 commit) is deliberately NOT covered by a second mutant entry here -- test/mutants/run_mutant.py's scope check constrains a single patch to a single target_file, and WtmApiClientAuthorizationHeaderLogLeakTests982 already exercises that file's fix directly (its own leak/positive-control tests), so a second mutant would add gate runtime without adding coverage this direct test does not already provide -- same reasoning #979 itself used for the same file.
target_symbol: WTMContext.CallAPI<T>(...) -- the Authorization add-point's inner `catch (FormatException ex)` block's `throw new InvalidOperationException(...)`, line ~97

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Security.WtmCo: to contain "s3cr3t-remotetoken-A1B2C3-do-not-log-me" because the secret must never reach the log

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed:
Captured from an actual `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant 982-callapi-authorization-header-exception-leak-reintroduce` run (builds/tests at -c Release, per #959) against this exact patch/entry pair. Pattern is anchored on the single-line FluentAssertions suffix text rather than the multi-line exception dump, following the #961/#979 lesson that Python's `.` does not span newlines under re's default flags. The RED-before-fix message this pattern matches against (captured independently, before the mutant tooling ran, while proving the #982 fix's own RED-before-fix state) was: Did not expect string "CallAPI failed to 'http://test/api'
System.FormatException: The format of value 'Bearer s3cr3t-remotetoken-A1B2C3-do-not-log-me
X-Injected: evil' is invalid.
   at System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaderParser.ParseValue(...)
   at System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaders.ParseAndAddValue(...)
   at System.Net.Http.Headers.HttpHeaders.Add(...)
   at WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.WTMContext.CallAPI[T](...)" to contain "s3cr3t-remotetoken-A1B2C3-do-not-log-me" because the secret must never reach the log, whether via the message template or the logged exception's own text. -- the mutant's bare `throw;` reproduces this exact shape.
